docs.title: GeneFox CLI and MCP server
docs.text:
genefox is the headless GeneFox: a command-line tool and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. It shares the analysis code that the GeneFox iOS, macOS and Android apps run, so its numbers, figures, CSVs, recipes and reports come from the same code the app screens call.

There are two ways to use it:

  • CLI subcommands (catalog, validate, render, fetch, report export, curated, doctor, tools). Each one runs once and exits. See the CLI reference.
  • genefox mcp, an MCP server over stdio (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0). It lets an MCP client such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex or OpenCode run GeneFox analyses. See the MCP server guide.

docs.title: Relationship to the GeneFox app
docs.text: Each MCP tool runs the same code a GeneFox app screen runs, and returns that screen's numbers as JSON. Most tools also write a PNG figure and can write the screen's CSV, a GeneFox recipe, or a single-figure HTML document. The tool catalogue lists every tool and the screen it corresponds to.

docs.title: Free tools and Pro
docs.text: Most tools are free (plus optional legacy tools that take local paths or URLs). The server fails closed for GeneFox Pro: a Pro tool is listed and callable only with a live grant, and nothing a client sends can grant one. See Entitlements.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Resource, cache and output directories are described in Install & resources.

docs.title: Subcommands and exit codes
docs.text:
Exit codes are 0 for success, 1 for a failure the command reports as error: <sentence> on stderr, and 64 for a usage error. The table lists, per subcommand, which conditions give which code.

Invocation Exit codes genefox (no arguments), genefox help, --help, -h 0: prints usage to stdout. genefox <unknown> 64: unknown command: <name>, then usage, on stderr. genefox catalog [--json] 0. genefox validate <recipe.json> 0 on success; 64 for a missing or extra argument; 1 when the file is missing or invalid. genefox render … 0 on success; 64 for a usage error; 1 for other failures. genefox fetch <url> … 0 on success; 64 for a usage error or a bad -m; 1 for a transport or decompression error. genefox report export … 0 on success; 1 for every failure, including argument errors. genefox doctor [--resources <dir>] [--output-dir <dir>] 0 when healthy; 1 if a required check fails; 64 for a usage error. Diagnostics go to stdout. genefox curated validate <dir> [--json] 0 when the dataset package is valid; 1 when it has issues (printed as file:line:column: message [code], or as the JSON report with --json); 1 for a usage error. genefox curated dose <view> <package-dir> [flags] The genefox run dose_response result: 0 on success; 1 when refused (no live Dose-Response grant, an unknown name, a package that fails its pins, a path outside the read root); 64 for a usage error. See the MCP server guide. genefox tools 0; 64 if any argument is given. genefox mcp [options] 64 for an option error; 0 when stdin reaches EOF and every in-flight call has answered; 0 when writing to stdout fails because the client has gone. genefox helper <command> The account helper's own exit codes: 2 for its usage. On macOS the command forwards to the signed helper binary, so its exit codes are the helper's; 1 when the helper is missing or its signature does not verify.

render treats a missing recipe, a second positional argument, an unrecognised option, or --r-script without --storage-dir as usage errors (64). Its --r-script combined with --size exits 1.

docs.title: genefox catalog [--json]
docs.text: Prints the operation catalogue (the same list list_operations returns): id, display name, summary and data scope. --json prints the same records as sorted, pretty-printed JSON, in the same form the MCP list_operations tool returns.

docs.title: genefox validate <recipe.json>
docs.text: Decodes a recipe store file (the JSON file GeneFox writes when you save recipes), validates every recipe and resolves its operation. It prints one line per recipe: validated: <name> — dataset <catalog>/<id>, operation <id>. Entries this build cannot read are counted and reported, never silently dropped. The CLI does not enforce the store's envelope-level policy (format id, version, caps). The legacy MCP tool validate_recipe gives the same verdict.

docs.title: genefox render <recipe.json> [options]
docs.text:
Replays the first recipe in the file and writes a PNG, or with --r-script, R source.

Option Meaning --storage-dir <dir> A local imported-dataset store. Required for imported recipes and for --r-script. --size <preset> single_column, one_and_a_half_column, double_column, slide or poster. Without it, a public recipe uses its recorded figure size, or double_column if it has none, and an imported recipe uses double_column. Rejected with --r-script. --r-script Emit the exact-input R script for an imported heatmap, signature or differential-expression recipe, instead of a PNG. -o <file> Write to this file and print wrote N bytes PNG (or … R source). Without -o, the bytes go to stdout. Overwrites.

Imported recipes replay from the verified local store. Public-dataset recipes replay through the MCP tools' shared runners (network access needed) into a private temporary directory, which is removed afterwards. They also need resources and a font that passes its pin. A destination with no verifiable PNG replay refuses. The size is capped at 8,192 px per side and 16,000,000 px in total.

docs.title: genefox fetch <url> [-o <file>] [-z] [-m <bytes>]
docs.text: Fetches a URL through the CLI's unrestricted transport (the MCP server's host allowlist does not apply here) and prints the body, or writes it with -o (overwrites). -z gunzips the response. -m is the maximum response size in bytes: default 50,000,000, allowed range 1 to 100,663,296. A value outside that range exits 64.

docs.title: genefox report export <file> [options]
docs.text:
Reads a saved GeneFox v1/v2 report, renders it through the PDF assembly the apps use, and writes it create-only to the output directory. It then prints wrote N bytes PDF to <path>.

Option Meaning --format pdf The only format accepted. --output-dir <dir> Output directory (see Output files); or GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR. --resources <dir> Authoritative report assets; or GENEFOX_RESOURCES, then install-prefix/app-bundle discovery. Uses bundled report assets when no scientific root is selected. --generated-at <ISO8601> Fixed document timestamp with a time zone (years 0001–9999), for reproducible bytes. --without-methods Omit the auto-generated Methods pages.

The report path must be a regular file, not a symbolic link, and fit this process's memory-derived size limit. Unreadable figures, invalid figure sizes, or tables over the budget refuse with no partial PDF written.

docs.title: genefox curated validate <dir> [--json]
docs.text: Checks a curated dataset package (manifest, columns dictionary, expression matrices and tables). Nothing is fetched and nothing is written.

docs.title: genefox curated dose <view> <package-dir> [flags]
docs.text: GeneFox Pro's dose-response analyses on an assembled curated package (resource.json, tables/<id>.tsv.gz, metadata.tsv), the same calls the app's dose panes make. Views: curve (also table: one compound's IC50 and AUC per line, refit and published side by side, and a line's curve), by_group, waterfall, volcano, mechanism, heatmap (the --top most informative compounds, --rank variation|strength, x the lines for the measure: --measure log10_ic50 --ic50 absolute|relative, auc or amax; lines grouped by --column; --scale z_score standardizes per compound; a hatched cell is not reached, gray is not tested; --style dots draws the same matrix as dots, colour log10 IC50 and size Amax in % effect, a hollow dot a fitted-asymptote Amax, an outlined dot not reached), biomarkers (one compound against every gene: --test expression Spearman or --test mutation Wilcoxon mutant vs wild-type, BH across the family, n per test, at least 6 lines or 3 per group; --direction gene --gene G for one gene against every compound; published values by default), single_dose_ranked, single_dose_by_group, single_dose_volcano, single_dose_bridge. Every grouping view groups by --column, or by a gene: --group-by expression --gene G [--split median|tertiles] or --group-by mutation --gene G (the package's variant table), or by stratify_derived (an annotation column or expression:G). The package's matrix.gfxm supplies expression. Flags: --compound, --line, --column, --control, --group-1, --group-2, --measure auc|log10_ic50|amax, --source refit|published (volcano, mechanism and heatmap default to published when the package has it), --ic50 absolute|relative, --fdr, --plot strip|box, --scale z_score|median|value, --top, --rank, --style cells|dots, --table, --limit, --figure true|false, --size, --format png|svg|tiff|pdf, --csv, --output-dir. The result is JSON: the pane's table, the Methods sentence with each table's own credit, the dose method hints, and the figure and CSV paths. The package directory is also the read root for the call. Without a live Dose-Response grant the tool is not offered and the command exits 1 (this headless build links no account, so it fails closed everywhere today).

docs.title: genefox doctor [--resources <dir>] [--output-dir <dir>]
docs.text:
Runs offline startup checks and prints one line per check: the scientific resource inventory and Ensembl reference (found/missing and path), bundled report marks and fonts (found/missing and path), the figure font's SHA-256 pin, an actual create-only write under the output root, the digest/inflate/transport seams and remaining required seams, an informational line of the should/pro/optional seams this host leaves uninstalled (never a failure), and the sorted MCP fetch allowlist. The write probe is removed afterwards. genefox fetch remains unrestricted.

Use --resources <dir> (or GENEFOX_RESOURCES) for scientific resources that are not installed beside the binary. Explicit resources are authoritative for report assets too. --output-dir wins over GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR, then defaults to <system temp>/genefox-mcp; a missing output directory is created under the usual output policy. A missing or corrupt resource, font-pin mismatch, failed write, or missing required seam exits 1; all checks passing exits 0. A malformed option exits 64. Missing-resource diagnostics name the manifest, reference or report asset that failed.

docs.title: genefox tools
docs.text: Prints the MCP tool catalogue as a markdown table: every tool this build registers, its access class (free, Pro or legacy) and its deadline. The tool catalogue is generated from this output.

docs.title: genefox mcp [options]
docs.text:
Serves MCP over stdio. Requests go in on stdin and responses come out on stdout; logs go to stderr. File descriptor 1 is pointed at stderr so that a stray print cannot corrupt the protocol stream.

Option Meaning --resources <dir> Scientific resources (see the install guide); or GENEFOX_RESOURCES, then resolved install prefix, then app bundle. --cache-dir <dir> Download cache; or GENEFOX_CACHE_DIR. Default: the native caches directory plus GeneFoxCLI (~/Library/Caches/GeneFoxCLI, or $XDG_CACHE_HOME/GeneFoxCLI on Linux). Available on every subcommand. --output-dir <dir> Where figures, CSVs, recipes and HTML are written; or GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR. Default <system temp>/genefox-mcp. --enable-legacy-tools Also list report_export_pdf, report_export_html, validate_recipe, fetch_url and render_recipe. These take local paths or URLs. --imported-store <dir> The local imported-dataset store that the legacy render_recipe may read for imported recipes. Only this flag names it; no tool argument can. --allow-root <dir> An extra local read root for the legacy validate_recipe/render_recipe paths, repeatable; or GENEFOX_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS (path-separated). The output directory and the imported store are always roots; a model-named path outside every root is refused. --warm <list> Comma-separated background prefetch: toil, pancan, or project ids the tools accept (for example TCGA-BRCA). Unknown tokens are logged and skipped. Skipped entirely without resources. --call-timeout <seconds> One deadline, from 1 to 3600 seconds, for every call, replacing each tool's own. --max-concurrent-calls <n> How many tools/calls run at once, from 1 to 64 (default: half the processors, at least 2 and at most 4). Up to 16 more queue; beyond that a call answers rate_limited (retryable).

A flag that takes a value refuses a following argument that starts with --. Every option error exits 64 and prints the usage line on stderr.

docs.title: Showing only some groups: keep_groups
docs.text: geo_series_expression, geo_gene_correlation, tcga_expression, geo_sample_pca, tcga_sample_pca and reference_ccle_expression take keep_groups: the levels of the figure's factor to show (the grouping, or a scatter's colour; tcga_expression takes keep_color_groups for its correlation scatter). Levels are matched exactly, as R's %in% matches them, and dropped levels are gone, as droplevels drops them: r, r², n, the group test and its degrees of freedom are recomputed on the retained samples (a PCA is re-solved on them). A level the data no longer has is refused, never ignored. The result's data.subset carries the engine's sentence ("Showing k of m groups: ...; statistics recomputed on the n retained samples."), which the recipe and HTML export also carry; GEO level names go under untrusted_*. No deep link is returned for a filtered figure, since a link cannot record the filter; the recipe does.

docs.title: Install & resources
docs.text:
Download

Get the CLI from the GeneFox download page.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
genefox targets these architectures. Availability depends on the published release:

  • macOS (universal: Apple silicon and Intel).
  • Linux (x86_64 and arm64), including Windows Subsystem for Linux.
  • Windows (x86_64), as genefox.exe.

docs.title: Installing the binary
docs.text:
Copy the binary to any directory on your PATH, together with SwiftPM's resource bundle: it holds the bundled report fonts and marks (see Bundled report resources). On macOS the bundle is locus_genefox.bundle, beside the binary. On Linux it is locus_genefox.bundle or locus_genefox.resources; genefox accepts either name. If the bundle is missing, genefox still runs, but report export refuses with a "resource unavailable" sentence instead of drawing substitute artwork.

If a file named genefox.commit sits beside the binary, the server reports its version as 1.1.0+<commit>, using that file's first 64 characters or fewer. Otherwise it reports 1.1.0+unknown.

docs.title: Install layout
docs.text:
Resource discovery expects a prefix laid out like this:

<prefix>/bin/genefox
<prefix>/bin/locus_genefox.bundle        # or locus_genefox.resources
<prefix>/share/genefox/Resources/
<prefix>/share/genefox/GeneFoxCLI-ThirdParty-NOTICE.txt  # when available

Add <prefix>/bin to PATH; resource discovery also works through a symlink to that binary.

docs.title: The macOS app's copy
docs.text:
The macOS app embeds genefox at GeneFox.app/Contents/Helpers/genefox, so a Mac App Store user needs no separate install. That copy runs in its own App Sandbox, as com.vds.GeneFox.cli (com.vds.GeneFox.cli.dev in development builds):

  • It reads its scientific resources from the app's locus_Locus.bundle and its report resources from Contents/Resources/locus_genefox.bundle. The sandbox lets it read the bundle only when the app is in /Applications.
  • It can read and write only its own container and the GeneFox group container, ~/Library/Group Containers/6NXG8V2R8W.com.vds.GeneFox. A path from your working directory fails, and the error says why. Its default output directory is that container's Agent Output folder.
  • genefox.commit sits in Contents/Resources, since Contents/Helpers holds only code.

docs.title: Scientific resources (--resources <dir> / GENEFOX_RESOURCES)
docs.text:
The analysis tools need the app's bundled scientific resources: a copy of the app's scientific resources directory. Name the directory with --resources <dir> (mcp, doctor and report export) or with GENEFOX_RESOURCES (every subcommand). The flag wins over the variable; a leading ~ is expanded. The complete lookup order is:

  1. --resources <dir>.
  2. GENEFOX_RESOURCES.
  3. <resolved executable directory>/../share/genefox/Resources (install prefix).
  4. For <X>.app/Contents/Helpers/genefox or Contents/MacOS/genefox, the app's Contents/Resources.
  5. None.

Executable symlinks are resolved before automatic lookup. Automatic candidates must contain an existing regular, non-symlink ScientificResources.json; a bare directory is ignored. Explicit flag/environment roots remain authoritative even if missing or corrupt. A corrupt manifest in a selected automatic root also fails integrity checks; it does not trigger a fallback to another root. Every source uses the same checks below.

genefox loads files from that directory only under these rules:

  • Names and types. A name must match [A-Za-z0-9._-], have at most 80 bytes and contain no ... The extension must be json, ttf, txt or png.
  • File type and size. Symbolic links and non-regular files are refused, and so is any file over 16 MB.
  • Integrity. ScientificResources.json has a compiled-in self-pin, and every listed file's size and SHA-256 are checked before the inventory reports available.
  • Font pin. The figure font SourceSans3-Regular.ttf is not in the manifest, so the server pins its SHA-256 itself. If the font loads but fails the pin, figures are still drawn, but each one reports parity: "font_mismatch".

At startup, genefox mcp logs one line to stderr with resources=/path (flag|environment|install-prefix|app-bundle) and the existing inventory=… reference=… font=… pin=… fields. It also reports cache=/path. Without usable resources, for example:

genefox mcp: pid=111 resources=none inventory=loaderUnavailable reference=unavailable font=missing pin=mismatch cache=/home/user/.cache/GeneFoxCLI out=/tmp/gfout allowlist=on legacy=off deadline=per-tool calls=4 queue=16 entitlement=free(not-linked) flavor=release version=1.1.0+unknown
genefox mcp: resources not ready; start the server with --resources <dir>

If the named directory does not exist, the server logs that too. It never fails to start. Without resources:

  • Gene tools. They stay listed but answer resource_unavailable. A missing reference is never reported as a missing gene.
  • Figures. With no font, no figure is drawn: the result carries figure_unavailable: "font not loaded", and the numbers still come back.
  • --warm. Skipped.
  • render. Refuses public and imported recipes ("The validated public-analysis resources and figure font are required.", or "The bundled figure font is unavailable.").

docs.title: Bundled report resources
docs.text:
The locus_GenefoxTools resource bundle holds the report brand marks (GeneFoxReportMark256.png, GeneFoxReportMark2400.png, VDSLogoFullColor.png, VDSLogoSymbol.png), the PDF fonts (SourceSans3-Regular, -Semibold, -Bold, LiberationSans-Regular, -Bold, -Italic) and their licence files. report export and the legacy report_export_pdf tool use these by default.

A selected scientific resources directory (explicit or automatically discovered) is authoritative for reports. If a brand mark or font is missing there, or cannot be decoded, the export refuses with resource_unavailable and writes no PDF. The bundled copies are never substituted.

docs.title: Download cache (--cache-dir <dir> / GENEFOX_CACHE_DIR)
docs.text:
Every subcommand accepts --cache-dir <dir> after the command name. It wins over GENEFOX_CACHE_DIR; leading ~ and relative paths are expanded at launch. Without either, the cache is the native host's default: Foundation's caches directory plus GeneFoxCLI, which is ~/Library/Caches/GeneFoxCLI on macOS and $XDG_CACHE_HOME/GeneFoxCLI (or ~/.cache/GeneFoxCLI) on Linux.

Download and curated payload caches use the override to resolve storage paths. Private store locations remain under GeneFoxCLI's native application-support root. The MCP startup line reports cache=/path, and doctor reports cache root: path=/path. This names the configured root; it does not probe cache write permissions. For containers, mount a persistent cache volume and pass its directory. On WSL, use the Linux filesystem rather than /mnt/c.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Figures, CSVs, recipes and HTML documents from mcp, and PDFs from report export, are written under one output directory that is fixed at launch:

  1. --output-dir <dir>, then GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR, then, for the macOS app's sandboxed copy only, ~/Library/Group Containers/6NXG8V2R8W.com.vds.GeneFox/Agent Output, then <system temp>/genefox-mcp.
  2. The directory is created with mode 0700 if missing. It must be a directory and must not be a symbolic link. Otherwise the MCP server reports out=unusable and file outputs come back as *_unavailable, while report export exits 1.

Every write follows these rules:

  • No paths from arguments. CSV and HTML names come from the app's own export name for that output; figure names come from the tool, the session's figure number and the title's slug, with an optional output_name stem. No tool argument becomes a path.
  • Name rules. A name that is not a plain file name falls back to a slug of letters, digits, ., _ and -. A plain name has no control or format characters, none of / \ : * ? " < > |, no leading ., - or space, no trailing . or space, and at most 200 bytes.
  • Create-only. A file is never overwritten. If the name is taken, the next candidate is <stem>-2.<ext>, <stem>-3.<ext> and so on, up to 1,000 attempts. The final write uses .withoutOverwriting, so a concurrent call that picked the same name moves on to the next suffix.
  • Containment. Every candidate must sit inside the output directory, compared component by component with this host's path convention, never as a string prefix. On Windows that comparison covers drive roots, UNC shares, both separators and case.
  • Windows device names. On every host, a name that is a Windows reserved device name (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-COM9, LPT1-LPT9, with or without an extension) is refused, because the file could later be copied to Windows.

MCP figure tools accept inline_image: true for clients that cannot read this directory. It adds an MCP image content item (data: base64 PNG, mimeType: image/png) when the written PNG is at most 1,048,576 bytes before encoding. Larger PNGs return no image item and disclose figure.inline_image_omitted with reason: "size_limit", bytes, and maximum_bytes: 1048576. Files are still written in both cases. Default is false, with the existing result bytes preserved when omitted. See coverage row E1 in list_coverage. The legacy render_recipe reports a render verdict and has no shared figure result.

The -o flags of render and fetch are different: they write the path you give, with a plain Data.write, and do overwrite an existing file.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
These are the environment variables the CLI reads:

Variable Read by Meaning GENEFOX_RESOURCES every subcommand Scientific/report resources directory, when no --resources flag is given; otherwise automatic install-prefix/app-bundle lookup. GENEFOX_CACHE_DIR every subcommand Download cache directory, when no --cache-dir flag is given. XDG_CACHE_HOME Linux cache default Base directory for the default GeneFoxCLI download cache (read by Foundation). GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR mcp, report export, doctor Output directory, when no --output-dir flag is given. GENEFOX_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS mcp Extra local read roots for the legacy path tools, path-separated (: on POSIX, ; on Windows); added to --allow-root. GENEFOX_TRANSPORT mcp, doctor record:<directory> or replay:<directory>; unset uses live transport. Invalid settings fail startup.

The default output directory comes from Foundation's FileManager.temporaryDirectory, which follows the platform's usual temporary-directory setting (for example TMPDIR on macOS and Linux).

docs.title: MCP transport cassettes
docs.text:
Start GENEFOX_TRANSPORT=record:./cassettes genefox mcp to wrap the existing host-allowlisted live transport. Start GENEFOX_TRANSPORT=replay:./cassettes genefox mcp to serve only recorded responses. Paths may be relative or begin with ~; the first colon separates mode from path. An unset variable uses live transport. Empty or invalid values exit 64 before the MCP server accepts input. doctor validates the same configuration. Tool provenance identifies the launch mode as live, record, or replay, including results served from memory. fetched_at remains the time the tool result was produced.

Cassette mode supports bounded in-memory responses. Disk-streaming downloads are refused rather than materialized in memory or sent through a live fallback; use live mode for those datasets. An isolated replay cache makes missing transport coverage visible.

Each request's filename is <sha256>.cassette, where SHA-256 covers the UTF-8 HTTP method, a newline, the absolute URL, a newline, and the raw request body (empty when absent). Headers do not enter the key. Streamed request bodies and bodies that cannot be checked as UTF-8 are refused. A replay miss fails with its key and URL and never contacts the network. Corrupt files, unreadable files and response size-limit failures also fail; they never fall through to live transport.

A cassette is one atomically written plain file. Its UTF-8 metadata is GENEFOX-CASSETTE-1 <status> <header-count> , then sorted lowercase name:value header lines, one blank line, then the exact binary response body. With zero headers, the count line is followed directly by the blank line. Only content-type, content-encoding, retry-after, etag, and last-modified are stored. Metadata is capped at 16 KiB; the caller's byte ceiling still applies to the body. Non-2xx responses are recorded and replayed with the shared HTTP status/retry policy. A repeated key replaces that file atomically; this is a response snapshot, not an ordered sequence of changing server answers.

Requests carrying Authorization, proxy authorization, cookies, or token/API-key/secret/ credential/password-looking headers are refused before a live call. URL credentials and credential-looking query/form/JSON fields (including NCBI api_key) are refused too. Request headers, URLs and bodies are never persisted; auth and cookie response headers are excluded. Cassettes retain the upstream response body verbatim, so use public-data tools and review response content before sharing recordings.

docs.title: Free enrichment of a precomputed DE table
docs.text:
genefox enrich complete.tsv --source "DE analysis export" --comparison "treated versus control" --complete-universe --output-dir ./reports uses the same imported_de_enrichment endpoint as the app's free Home entry and MCP. Input must be UTF-8 CSV/TSV with gene, log2FoldChange, and raw pValue columns, at least 500 distinct exact gene symbols, every tested gene including nonsignificant genes, at most 50,000 rows and 2 MiB. Source and comparison labels are limited to 200 UTF-8 bytes with no control characters. Symbols use exact ASCII spelling and column duplicate checks use exact UTF-8 identity. The declaration is the user's; GeneFox cannot verify completeness and does not recompute DE or infer sample sizes. Duplicate symbols, malformed rows, nonfinite effects and raw p outside (0,1] are refused without dropping genes.

The foreground contains up to 200 nonneutral genes per direction, adjustable with --foreground-size 1..200. Results retain each validated gene set, its overlap and expected overlap, conditional odds ratio and one-sided lower 95% bound, upper-tail p, BH q within direction, overlapping genes and unavailable reasons. Inf is an unbounded estimate/boundary. Every table records the declared background and source hash and carries the shared methods and membership provenance.

By default one multipart PDF, matching branded HTML and complete CSV are written create-only; JSON results and actual file descriptors go to stdout. Use --format pdf, html, csv, or none for explicit choices, and --generated-at <ISO8601> for a fixed shared timestamp. GENEFOX_RESOURCES selects an authoritative resource directory as for other commands. This full-table analysis is separate from the selected-gene matrix DE screen and its 80-gene limit.

docs.title: Run a tool directly
docs.text:
genefox run --list returns the same live tool list as MCP tools/list, including its current release, entitlement, legacy and model-tool filters. Any listed tool can be invoked through genefox run <tool> --json '<arguments>'. This calls the same request handler, deadlines, validation, access gates and output writer as genefox mcp; it has no separately maintained analysis dispatch table.

For example, genefox run list_operations lists operations, and genefox run tcga_expression --project TCGA-BRCA --gene TP53 --figure false uses schema-named flags. String arguments retain their exact spelling, including numeric identifiers; arrays and objects use JSON literals. Use --json for a complete argument object, and do not mix it with individual tool flags. Repeated tool arguments are refused. Host options such as --resources, --output-dir, --cache-dir and --enable-legacy-tools work before or after the tool name.

Stdout is one MCP result object, including content and optional error status, or the RPC error object for an unavailable tool. Diagnostics and notifications go to stderr. Exit codes are 0 for success, 1 for a tool/RPC failure, 64 for invalid CLI usage, and 78 for an unusable resource folder. Each invocation owns a fresh session: conversations or other handles spanning calls use genefox mcp.

docs.title: Measured method hints
docs.text:
GEO expression and sample PCA may add data.method_hints. These are deterministic advice derived from already available full-source library sizes and low-depth flags. Each item has a stable code, advisory_only: true, a message, measured evidence, and suggested recommended_arguments when applicable. The existing normalization, values, exclusions and captions remain the authoritative result; hints never rerun analysis, change methods, exclude samples or call a model.

A figure whose value axis went to scientific notation over values that are all zero or more adds figure.method_hints with code axis_log_scale: its axis, range and tick labels as evidence, and recommended_arguments (for example value_scale: log10) only where this tool lists that scale and Publication Studio is granted. The figure is drawn as asked.

count_depth_normalization suggests reviewing log_cpm for unprocessed integer read/probe counts when source depths differ more than10-fold or low-depth samples are flagged. Its normalization_applied: false refers to the recommendation; it does not erase any transform explicitly requested for the result. low_depth_samples suggests reviewing the disclosed threshold and explicit exclude_low_depth when flagged samples remain included. pca_library_size_qc asks for a PC1/log-library-size check and explicitly states that this association has not been calculated by the hint. Zero source depth yields a null fold range, with zero_library_count retained, never infinity or a fabricated finite ratio. Integer-count eligibility does not identify the biological assay; source-published processing, including nCounter assay controls, must be respected. Guidance and evaluation cases live in the agent plugin's shared method-choice reference.

docs.title: Public GEO heatmaps
docs.text:
geo_heatmap exposes the app's public GEO heatmap through MCP and the generated Python/R clients. For a one-shot CLI call, use the shared genefox run dispatcher:

genefox run geo_heatmap --json '{"accession":"GSE119933","probes":["1368934_at","1370269_at"],"annotations":["compound"],"group_by":"compound","keep_groups":["Wy","Ibup"],"z_normalize":true,"cluster_columns":false,"csv":true}' --output-dir ./figures

The compatibility spelling genefox geo-heatmap --arguments <JSON> retains its plain JSON result and delegates execution to the shared native SDK session.

Genes resolve through the platform annotation; ambiguous symbols require exact probes. Missing requested probes and cells are disclosed. Sample filters recompute normalization and clustering on the retained samples; count normalization retains full-source library sums across all rows. Exact identifiers are never case-folded or silently deduplicated. The app's shared heatmap analysis, annotation colors, trees and figure exporter draw the result. Single-strip raw/log2/TPM exports are byte-identical to the app's export for the same matrix and controls. Multiple strips and count-normalized input use that same engine, with the interface difference disclosed. GEO heatmap recipes remain unavailable, matching the app's in-memory series pane. The CSV uses the app's bounded displayed-cell projection and reports its unavailability above the portable export limit.

docs.title: Rich shell arguments and schema help
docs.text:
genefox run <tool> --help shows the arguments from that tool's live schema, including required fields, defaults, types and descriptions. Hidden tools receive exactly the same refusal as unknown names. Help does not need scientific resources.

Flags accept --second-gene TP53 or --second_gene=TP53. A bare boolean flag means true; --figure=false supplies false. Repeat array flags or use comma-separated items (--genes TP53,ESR1 --genes BRCA1); a JSON array preserves commas inside an individual value. String identifiers retain leading zeros and their original spelling. The shared tool validator still decides whether values are valid.

Use one --args-file /path/arguments.json instead of individual flags or --json for a bounded UTF-8 JSON object read through the native regular-file reader. Directories, non-regular files, oversized inputs, excessive nesting and malformed JSON are refused before host startup. A bare --json is also accepted as an alias for the default MCP output, including with --list.

The default stdout remains the complete MCP result/error object and the standard exit contract remains 0 (success), 1 (tool/RPC failure), 64 (usage), 78 (resources). Python/R integrations need no changes. --result-format text explicitly selects text content or a readable tool list. When text omits inline non-text content, stderr identifies the omission; --result-format mcp retains every item.

Opt in to --exit-codes classified for 2 (invalid arguments), 3 (gate/policy refusal or unavailable tool), 4 (upstream/network/timeout failure), and 1 (other tool failures). Unlisted/new tool error codes keep exit 1. Command-line usage and resource startup errors remain 64 and 78. This recovers the historical rich CLI capabilities while preserving the current SDK transport defaults.

docs.title: MCP server guide
docs.text:
genefox mcp serves GeneFox's analyses to an MCP client over stdio. Each tool runs the same analysis code a GeneFox app screen runs, and returns that screen's numbers as JSON. Most tools also write a PNG figure and can write the screen's CSV, a GeneFox recipe, or a single-figure HTML document.

See Install & resources and the CLI reference.

docs.title: Starting the server
docs.text:
genefox mcp --resources /path/to/Resources --output-dir ~/genefox-out
Option Meaning --resources <dir> A copy of the app's scientific resources directory; or GENEFOX_RESOURCES, then <resolved executable directory>/../share/genefox/Resources, then <X>.app/Contents/Resources for a Contents/Helpers/genefox or Contents/MacOS/genefox executable. Automatic roots require ScientificResources.json; every source uses the same integrity checks. With no folder, a missing one, or one without ScientificResources.json, the server does not start (status 78, the reason on stderr). If its digests or the gene reference then fail the background check, gene tools answer resource_unavailable naming the reason, and no figure is drawn. --cache-dir <dir> Download cache; or GENEFOX_CACHE_DIR. Default ~/Library/Caches/GeneFoxCLI on macOS, $XDG_CACHE_HOME/GeneFoxCLI (or ~/.cache/GeneFoxCLI) on Linux. Mount a persistent volume in containers; on WSL prefer the Linux filesystem. --output-dir <dir> Where figures, CSVs, recipes and HTML are written; or set GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR. Default <system temp>/genefox-mcp. Files are only ever created there, never overwritten. --enable-legacy-tools Also list the five legacy tools, which take local paths or URLs. --imported-store <dir> The imported-dataset store the legacy render_recipe may read. A tool argument cannot name a store. --allow-root <dir> An extra local read root for the legacy validate_recipe/render_recipe paths, repeatable; or GENEFOX_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS (path-separated). The output directory and the imported store are always roots; a model-named path outside every root is refused. --warm <list> Prefetch toil, pancan and/or project ids such as TCGA-BRCA, in the background. --call-timeout <seconds> One deadline (1–3600 s) for every call, replacing each tool's own. --help, -h Print the usage and exit 0. --max-concurrent-calls <n> How many tools/calls run at once (1–64; default half the processors, 2 to 4). Up to 16 more queue; beyond that a call answers rate_limited. See Limits.

An option error exits with status 64, and a missing resources folder with status 78, before the server reads any input. Otherwise the server prints one self-check line to stderr and then serves until stdin closes, for example:

genefox mcp: pid=152 resources=/path/to/Resources (flag) inventory=available reference=available font=ok pin=ok cache=/home/user/.cache/GeneFoxCLI out=/tmp/gfout allowlist=on legacy=off deadline=per-tool calls=4 queue=16 entitlement=free(not-linked) flavor=release version=1.1.0+unknown

Some fields in that line need explanation:

  • allowlist=on: in mcp mode the network transport admits only an exact list of public-data hosts, over HTTPS on port 443, and re-checks every redirect. PedcBioPortal, loopback and GeneFox's own cloud hosts are deliberately absent.
  • entitlement=free(not-linked): see Entitlements.

Progress. A tools/call whose request carries params._meta.progressToken gets a notifications/progress every 10 seconds until it answers, with the seconds elapsed as progress (no total: a call cannot know its own length), so a client that resets its timeout on progress keeps waiting through a slow first call. Without a token nothing is sent; each slow tool's description gives its expected time.

Stdout carries only protocol messages. Logs, including one genefox mcp: host_not_allowed … line per refused request, go to stderr.

docs.title: Connecting a client
docs.text:
Every client starts the server the same way: it runs the command genefox mcp [options] and talks to it over stdin and stdout. Use absolute paths, because a client may start the server from any working directory.

Long calls need a long client timeout. The server's own deadlines are 300 s, or 900 s for the slow tools (see Limits), and a cold first call can take minutes. Several clients stop waiting sooner than that by default; each client section below says how to raise its limit.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
claude mcp add --transport stdio genefox --scope user \
  --env GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR=$HOME/genefox-out \
  -- /usr/local/bin/genefox mcp --resources /path/to/Resources

Or commit a project-scoped .mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "genefox": {
      "command": "/usr/local/bin/genefox",
      "args": ["mcp", "--resources", "/path/to/Resources"],
      "env": { "GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR": "/Users/you/genefox-out" }
    }
  }
}

Claude Code reads these timeout settings, all in milliseconds:

  • MCP_TIMEOUT limits server startup.
  • MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT, or a per-server "timeout" in .mcp.json, limits a single tool call.

Check the Claude Code MCP documentation for the current defaults.

docs.title: Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Claude Desktop uses the same mcpServers shape, in claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "genefox": {
      "command": "/usr/local/bin/genefox",
      "args": ["mcp", "--resources", "/path/to/Resources", "--output-dir", "/Users/you/genefox-out"]
    }
  }
}

I could not verify the file's location or Claude Desktop's tool-call timeout here; check Claude Desktop's documentation for both.

docs.title: Codex
docs.text:
codex mcp add genefox --env GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR=$HOME/genefox-out \
  -- /usr/local/bin/genefox mcp --resources /path/to/Resources

Or in ~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.genefox]
command = "/usr/local/bin/genefox"
args = ["mcp", "--resources", "/path/to/Resources"]
env = { GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR = "/Users/you/genefox-out" }
startup_timeout_sec = 30
tool_timeout_sec = 960

Codex documents defaults of startup_timeout_sec = 10 and tool_timeout_sec = 60. A 60-second tool timeout ends most cold GeneFox calls early, so raise it as shown. Check Codex's documentation for the current keys.

docs.title: OpenCode
docs.text:
In opencode.json (or opencode.jsonc):

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "genefox": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["/usr/local/bin/genefox", "mcp", "--resources", "/path/to/Resources"],
      "environment": { "GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR": "/Users/you/genefox-out" },
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 960000
    }
  }
}

OpenCode's per-server timeout is in milliseconds; its documented default is 5000. In OpenCode 1.18.34 it bounds every request to the server, tool calls included, not only the tool listing: a 75-second call is cut off at "timeout": 60000 with MCP error -32001: Request timed out, and completes at "timeout": 960000 . Set it to 960000 so the 900 s tools can finish.

docs.title: Protocol surface
docs.text:
The server speaks protocol version 2024-11-05 and reports the server as genefox version 1.1.0. Each line on stdin is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, and each response is one line on stdout. The server handles these messages:

Message Behaviour initialize Returns capabilities: {tools: {}}, serverInfo and instructions: the usage rules a model should follow, which summarise this guide. ping Returns {}. tools/list The tools this process may offer (see Entitlements and Legacy tools). The list and the dispatcher read the same registry, so a listed tool is always callable. tools/call Runs a tool. Its result is one text content item holding the tool's JSON. isError: true means the tool ran and reports a tool error. notifications/cancelled Cancels the call named by requestId. The cancelled call writes no response. any other id-less message Silence. any other method JSON-RPC error -32601.

docs.title: Tool catalogue
docs.text: See the generated tool catalogue.

docs.title: Argument conventions
docs.text:
TCGA/GDC human gene inputs use GeneFox's existing approved-symbol and curated-alias reference: for example, Her2 resolves to ERBB2 and PD-L1 to CD274. An approved symbol takes precedence over an alias. Imported feature IDs and GEO probes retain their literal spelling and organism-specific meaning.

Cohort expression, gene signatures, heatmaps and differential panels return data.gene_resolution: the original token, canonical symbol, exact dataset field, dataset version, mapping release and source checksums. GDC STAR expression uses the verified annotation declared by the dataset sidecar. A custom loader's unknown mapping source is represented as null. Provider-supplied dataset versions use the bounded untrusted_dataset_version key; reports and CSV retain the complete version. With csv: true, these tools also write gene_resolution_csv; the primary data CSV keeps its existing columns. Captured reports retain the mapping provenance, and saved views retain the requested tokens.

gene_info accepts a symbol or a quoted Entrez ID and supports human genes only. A numeric ID must match the final human record exactly; a different or redirected record is refused as gene_identity_mismatch. A genuine missing record is gene_not_found; malformed or incomplete upstream metadata is upstream_malformed. The returned symbol is NCBI's official name, while summary and aliases remain under untrusted_* keys.

Every tool reads its arguments under these rules:

  • Closed schemas. Every input schema has additionalProperties: false. An unknown key is refused with invalid_argument, naming the key in field, so a misspelt key is reported instead of silently changing the analysis.
  • null means absent. For an optional field, an empty string (after trimming) also counts as absent.
  • Types. A wrong JSON type is refused with a sentence such as gene: expected a string, got a number. JSON true decodes as a boolean, not as the number 1.
  • Strings are trimmed, then checked against a maximum length and, where the tool has one, a whole-string pattern. A TCGA gene symbol must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*$, with at most 30 characters, and is upper-cased as the TCGA screens do. The GTEx gene is trimmed but not upper-cased, as that screen does.
  • Enumerations must be one of the listed values. A project id is matched case-insensitively and answered in canonical form (tcga-stad becomes TCGA-STAD).
  • Integers and numbers are checked as doubles before any conversion. A value must be finite and within the schema's minimum/maximum, and an integer must also be whole. A value out of range is refused, never clamped.
  • String lists are trimmed and de-duplicated case-insensitively. A list over its maximum count is refused, never truncated.
  • Figure size. A tool with a size argument also accepts width_in, height_in, dpi (72–1,200) and the figure-style keys (survival_detail, show_row_counts, show_caption_color_keys, show_figure_legends). A custom size must stay within the app's side limits, 8,192 px per side and 16 megapixels in total. dpi is accepted only together with width_in and height_in.
  • Figure file name. A tool with a size argument also accepts output_name, a stem for the figure's file name in place of the tool name and the title's slug. It takes letters, digits, ., _ and -, starts with a letter or digit, and is at most 64 characters. A name with a separator (/, \, :), a .., or any other character is refused before the tool runs. Only the figure's descriptive part changes; see Figures.
  • A heatmap opened from a differential-expression result (from_differential_expression) records its comparison and top_n in its deep_link and recipe (de: and de_top: flags). open_destination and a recipe replay reopen it as one: the comparison is rerun and its top genes taken again over its samples under the DE group strip, as the apps reopen it; a recipe flag this build cannot read runs nothing. A comparison by molecular subtype does not draw the default Subtype strip beside the DE group strip that already shows it.
  • Figure axes (GeneFox Pro). The tools whose figures have continuous axes also accept x_min, x_max, x_scale, y_min, y_max, y_scale, value_min, value_max and value_scale, each tool only for the axes its figures have: x and y for a scatter or volcano (geo_gene_correlation, tcga_top_correlates, geo_top_correlates, tcga_differential_expression, and the PC1 x PC2 scatter of tcga_sample_pca and geo_sample_pca, which refuse a customization with biplot, scree or correlated_genes, whose figures have no customizable axis), value for a box, violin or strip (tcga_tumor_normal, tcga_pan_cancer_expression, tcga_compare_cohorts, reference_treehouse_expression, gtex_tissue_expression, cbioportal_expression), and the axes of whichever figure figure_kind or the grouping draws (tcga_expression: all three; tcga_gene_signature: x for the histogram, value for the grouped box; geo_series_expression: x for the ungrouped histogram, value for a one-factor box, violin or strip (tcga_expression's ecdf has no customizable axes), x and y for a continuous characteristic's scatter, none for a two-factor view; without geometry a value key means the box and an x or y key the scatter, and a characteristic the matrix shows to be the other kind is refused once it is read). A bound is a finite number in data units on either scale; a scale is linear (the default) or log10. A histogram's x bounds restrict its binning range. Values outside a bound, and values at or below zero on a log axis, are not drawn; the figure says how many in its caption and its description. A reversed range, a non-positive bound on a log axis, an axis the figure does not have, or a figure kind with no customizable axis (a survival curve, a two-factor box, an ECDF) is refused with invalid_argument. Every one of these keys is Pro (publicationStudio) and refused with entitlement_required unless the server's context grants that capability (see Entitlements). A customization is saved with what the call writes: a recipe records it as one axes: flag on its destination (the same keys, axes:value_min=7;value_max=12;value_scale=linear) and in its presentation metadata, whose Methods line names the axes; open_destination and genefox render pass a recorded flag back to the tool, so a replay draws the same axes and stays Pro-gated, and a flag this build cannot read runs nothing. A CSV is the data, unchanged (csv.customization and csv.customization_note say so); an HTML document embeds the customized engine figure (html.parity: app_document_engine_figure); figure: false returns the data and echoes customization with a customization_note. Significance brackets on a customized value axis test the values it shows, on its scale, as ggplot2 does. A caption that cannot fit, or would squeeze the plot, is refused with the size that would work; it is never cropped. A drawn customized figure reports figure.customization (the value's stable JSON) and parity: engine_only. genefox render takes the same values as --x-min, --x-scale and so on, for an imported plot or signature replay and for a signature's --r-script (x for the score histogram, value for the one-factor box plot). The script draws them as GeneFox does: values outside a bound, and values at or below zero on a log axis, are removed before anything is binned or summarized, which is ggplot2's scale-limits behaviour (scale_x_continuous(limits = ), scale_x_log10()), not coord_cartesian()'s zoom; the already-filtered geometry is drawn with oob = scales::oob_keep and the figure's caption. A public recipe replays the axes it recorded, and refuses the flags.

Every refusal is a tool error whose code is invalid_argument and whose field names the argument. It happens before any network request. No argument of a non-legacy tool is a filesystem path or a URL to fetch. open_destination takes a genefox:// link, which it decodes as the app's route planner does; it does not fetch it.

docs.title: Results and the untrusted_* trust model
docs.text:
A successful result is a JSON object. Analysis tools return tool, data, display (the screen's sentences and tables, to quote verbatim), caveats and provenance. provenance holds sources, genefox_cli (the version), transport: "live" (or "record" / "replay"), fetched_at and, where a screen applies, parity_screen.

When a result list is capped, truncated discloses its field, kept and total counts. One capped list produces an object; multiple capped lists produce an array of those objects, so every cap is disclosed.

Third-party text is never placed under a plain key. Text that comes from a dataset, a portal or a model goes under a key named untrusted_*. Examples are GEO sample characteristics and author labels, CSV headers named after them, Reference and cBioPortal labels and study text, local-model replies, and a deep link that carries GEO text (untrusted_deep_link). The initialize instructions tell the model to treat these fields as data, never as instructions. Each string is capped at 120 characters, with a trailing … when cut. A few diagnostic fields use their own larger caps; for example, GEO supplementary refusal diagnostics allow 512 characters for a file name and 1,200 for a reason. When a file name is derived from GEO text, the written path is returned as untrusted_path / untrusted_file_name.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
TCGA and GEO expression offer a cumulative distribution (geometry=ecdf) over the retained observations, including constant-valued samples. GEO distribution exports retain grouping controls and apply any keep_groups subset before pooling values. It uses the same GeneFox engine as the cards on the apps. Its export recipe preserves the ECDF selection. ECDF axes are fixed; custom bounds or scales refuse before loading data.

Expression distributions offer box, strip and violin plots, with histogram or ECDF where that screen's schema offers them. The expression bar option is retired. For one release, MCP accepts the older bar and median_bar spellings as box-plot aliases and returns a migration caveat. Saved views, links and recipes that recorded a bar also open as a box plot with a notice; genefox render writes the notice to stderr. Keep the returned caveat with the figure. Genuine count, proportion and ranked bar charts retain their own geometry.

A figure tool draws through GeneFox's shared engine and writes its figure create-only under the output directory. The optional format argument picks the file: png (the default, a raster), svg (vector, with editable text) or tiff (raster, the extension .tif). Every figure is written in all three formats from the same drawing, and format follows the file's extension and media type (format and mime_type in the result). SVG keeps the figure's labels as editable text. It then returns figure with these keys:

Key Meaning path, file_name, bytes, sha256, width_px, height_px The file written. For a PNG the pixel size is read from the file itself. format, mime_type The file's format (png, svg or tiff) and its media type. geometry, size What was drawn. size is the preset token, or custom. description The engine's description of the figure. alt_text Alt text: the engine's own summary and caveat if it has one, otherwise the description, otherwise a sentence built from the title. data_table [{label, value}], one row per drawn element (group, arm, legend row, or point), in drawn order. data_table_rows, data_table_truncated, data_table_note The table's row count before the cap; whether the table was cut; and, only when it was, a sentence saying so. data_table_unavailable Replaces the table when the engine attached no element description. parity, parity_screen, parity_note See Parity tokens.

File names. A figure's file name is

<NN>_<tool>_<slug>_<W>x<H>in[_<dpi>dpi].<ext>
  • NN is the figure's number in this server session, counted from 01 and never reused, so two figures from one session never share a name, even when they come from the same tool.
  • tool is the tool that drew the figure, and slug is the title's slug. output_name, when given, replaces tool_slug and nothing else.
  • W and H are the size in inches, to one decimal; dpi is the resolution. A vector file (svg) has no resolution, so its name has no _<dpi>dpi.
  • ext is the one extension the format takes: png, svg or tif.

Example: 01_tcga_pan_cancer_expression_box-plot_7.2x6.0in_300dpi.png.

A name that is already taken is never replaced. The file takes -2, -3 and so on before its extension, so 01_..._300dpi-2.png is the second file with that name.

The data table is capped at 200 rows. Only scatter and volcano figures, which have one row per point, reach that cap. Rows past it are not lost: they are still in the tool's data and CSV, which are never capped by this.

When a figure's labels are third-party text, description, alt_text and data_table are replaced by untrusted_description, untrusted_alt_text and untrusted_data_table, never returned beside them, and every cell is capped as above. The counts and the truncation note are GeneFox's own text and stay under plain keys.

A figure can also be missing:

  • figure_unavailable: no font, no output directory, nothing to draw, or a write failure.
  • figure_refused: the engine's refusal sentence.

The server never draws an unlabelled figure.

With inline_image: true, a figure tool also returns an MCP content item {"type":"image","data":"<base64 PNG>","mimeType":"image/png"} alongside the existing text item. The cap is 1,048,576 PNG bytes before base64 encoding, inclusive. For a larger PNG, no image item is returned; figure.inline_image_omitted contains {"reason":"size_limit","bytes":N,"maximum_bytes":1048576}. The PNG is still written create-only and its file metadata is still returned. The argument defaults to false; omitting it preserves the existing result bytes. This lets clients display figures without access to the server's output directory. An unavailable or refused figure adds no image content. The legacy render_recipe reports a render verdict and has no shared figure result.

With html: true, a tool also writes the screen's single-figure HTML document. That document's <img alt> is the figure's alt_text, and after the figure it has a "Figure 1 data" table of the same rows, with the same 200-row cap. Every string in it is HTML-escaped. If no figure was drawn, the result carries html_unavailable instead; tcga_case_expression always answers html_unavailable, with the reason, because its screen exports no HTML.

csv: true and recipe: true work the same way. They return csv or recipe (with path, bytes and sha256), or csv_unavailable / recipe_unavailable with a reason.

docs.title: Parity tokens
docs.text:
The figure.parity and html.parity fields say how an output relates to what the app exports:

Token Where Meaning app_export_identical figure.parity The app screen's PNG export calls the same shared function with the same arguments. engine_only figure.parity Drawn by the shared engine, but the screen has no PNG export to match; for example, the screen snapshots the view, or the figure was drawn with customized axes, which no screen draws yet. font_mismatch figure.parity Replaces either value above when the figure font failed its SHA-256 pin. The glyph widths may differ from the app's. app_document_engine_png html.parity The app's HTML document over the screen's title, subtitle, source and table, embedding the engine's PNG bytes. Apple re-encodes the same pixels. app_document_engine_figure html.parity As above, but the screen snapshots this figure, so the app's own document embeds a snapshot where this one embeds the engine figure.

The related fields are:

  • figure.parity_screen: names the app screen the figure corresponds to.
  • provenance.parity_screen: names the screen whose numbers the tool reproduces. The two can differ; for example, a Survival tab's numbers can come with an engine-drawn figure.
  • parity_note: a sentence stating exactly where the output departs from the app, where there is something to say.

docs.title: Entitlements (GeneFox Pro)
docs.text:
The server fails closed. Pro tools are listed and callable only when the server grants the required capability. Hidden tools answer -32602 Unknown tool. No argument, flag, environment variable or file grants Pro access.

Pro tools: batch_explorer_run, publication_studio_export, dataset_radar_check and dose_response. Without a live grant a Pro tool is not listed, and a direct call is refused with entitlement_required before any file is opened. genefox curated dose <view> <package-dir> runs dose_response from a terminal.

account_status reports linked: false, entitlement: "not_linked", granted_capabilities: [] and cloud_ai: "off", with the caveat "Linking a GeneFox account to this server is not available in this version."

lab_collaboration_status, cloud_sync_status, cloud_sync_now and cloud_sync_store are free. They need a linked account, so in this version they report that none is linked.

docs.title: Account and cloud authority
docs.text:
Account linking, cloud retry and the dataset finder are not available in this build:

  • Disabled by default. Each server context starts with an absent authority: no service, no profile, no evidence. No production tool creates a privileged publication, no MCP argument can supply a service, evidence or approval, and the authority is shut down at EOF.

  • One-use human approval. The design requires a decision made in the human helper's own interface for linking and for each cloud request. An approval is bound to one exact request, host and authority generation, and is consumed when used.

  • Model-run commands are never human approval. An agent running a terminal command, or a model setting a force-style flag, is not the human decision the design requires. No tool input can stand in for it.

Local conversations (tcga_ask_open, geo_ask_open, ask_turn, ask_close) use only a host-owned local model and execute no analysis on their own. local_model_status reports whether a local model is ready. On the Linux build it reports conversation: "unsupportedPlatform" and single_query: "unsupportedPlatform".

docs.title: Limits, deadlines and cancellation
docs.text:
Limit Value Behaviour Request line size 4 MB (maximumLineBytes) Refused before decoding: -32700 "Request line exceeds 4 MB", id null. JSON nesting depth 32 levels, the envelope counting as 1 (maximumNestingDepth) Refused before decoding: -32700 "Request nesting exceeds 32 levels", id null. Per-call deadline 300 s by default; 900 s for the slow tools; 30 s for ask_turn (see the catalogue) The call answers timed_out (retryable). The abandoned work may finish and fill the cache, so a retry is usually faster. --call-timeout 1–3600 s Replaces every tool's deadline. Concurrent calls (--max-concurrent-calls) 1–64; default half the processors, 2 to 4; 16 more may queue Beyond the queue: rate_limited (retryable, details.source: genefox_server), not run. Queued time counts against the deadline (timed_out with details.queued: true). Early cancellations remembered 256 A notifications/cancelled that arrives before its request is remembered, and that request is then dropped. GEO search cursors 32 active searches, 15-minute idle expiry, 5,000 results per search cursor_capacity (retryable), cursor_expired, cursor_busy (retryable), pagination_limit. Local conversations 2–8 sessions and 8–64 MB of snapshot memory in total, both measured from physical memory; 15-minute lifetime session_capacity, session_expired, session_busy (retryable).

The deadline timer is a Dispatch timer outside Swift's cooperative pool, so a saturated pool cannot delay the timed_out verdict.

Concurrency. The read loop starts one task per request line immediately, so ping and tools/list are never queued behind a slow analysis. Only tools/call passes the call limiter: at most --max-concurrent-calls run at once and up to 16 more wait, first come first served; a call beyond that answers rate_limited at once. A slot is held by the work, not the answer, so a timed-out or cancelled call keeps it until its kernel returns.

docs.title: JSON-RPC errors
docs.text: Code When -32700 Invalid JSON, a line over 4 MB, or nesting deeper than 32. Answered with id null. -32601 Unsupported method. -32602 tools/call named a tool that is not listed. For a legacy tool started without the flag, the message is Tool not available: <name> is a legacy tool; start the server with --enable-legacy-tools.

docs.title: Tool errors
docs.text:
A tool error is a normal tools/call result with isError: true, whose text is {"error": {"code", "message", "retryable", "field"?, "details"?}}. The codes used in this tree are:

Code Meaning invalid_argument An argument was refused (field names it), or an input file or report was unreadable. entitlement_required A GeneFox Pro argument (field) the context does not grant (details.capability); nothing was run. resource_unavailable The scientific resources, gene reference, or a report asset is missing. gene_not_found, ambiguous_gene The gene did not resolve, or resolved to more than one row (details lists the candidates). no_data, no_expression_data Nothing to analyse, or no expression matrix (GEO, Expression Atlas, supplementary files). not_runnable, unsupported_here, query_refused The analysis is refused with the app's sentence; the screen has no tool here; or the shared planner/validator refused the query. conflicting_loci, incomplete_family (retryable), upstream_partial_failure (retryable) Pan-cancer and pan-cancer survival assembly failures. upstream_unavailable (retryable), upstream_http (retryable for 5xx), rate_limited (retryable, retry_after), upstream_malformed, response_too_large Network and source failures. host_not_allowed The server reached a host outside the allowlist (details.host). seam_unavailable A platform seam was not installed. geo_search_failed, cursor_expired, cursor_busy, cursor_capacity, pagination_limit GEO search and pagination. session_capacity, session_expired, session_busy, session_limit, model_unavailable, invalid_model_response Local conversations. output_unavailable report_export_pdf has no usable output directory. timed_out (retryable, details.deadline_seconds), cancelled The deadline passed, or the call was cancelled. internal Anything else, with its message.

Some file outputs fail without failing the call. They are reported beside the result as figure_unavailable, csv_unavailable, recipe_unavailable or html_unavailable.

docs.title: Legacy tools
docs.text:
--enable-legacy-tools adds five tools that take a local path or a URL, which no other tool does:

  • report_export_pdf: a saved report to a PDF, written create-only to the output directory.
  • report_export_html: a saved report to one self-contained HTML document, written create-only to the output directory.
  • validate_recipe: the CLI's validate verdict.
  • fetch_url: fetches through the installed transport. In mcp mode that is the allowlisted transport. maximumBytes must be between 1 and 100,663,296, the default is 50 MB, and text over 100,000 bytes is returned as a preview.
  • render_recipe: the CLI's render. An imported recipe reads only the store the server was started with (--imported-store); the model cannot choose a store, and a storage_directory argument is refused.

Without the flag they are neither listed nor callable (-32602).

A legacy tool reports a failure as isError: true with a plain-text sentence beginning error:, not as the {"error": {...}} object described under Tool errors. For example, fetch_url to a host outside the allowlist answers error: The GeneFox MCP server does not contact <host>: it reaches only the public-data hosts its tools need., and the server logs genefox mcp: host_not_allowed request host=<host> to stderr.

docs.title: list_coverage
docs.text:
list_coverage takes no arguments. It returns one row per free app operation: row, operation, app_screen, mcp_tool (or null), status and note. The status is one of available, partial, planned or not_available_headless. The result also has counts per status. On this build, list_coverage reported 54 available, 17 partial, 12 planned and 6 not available headlessly. A final row summarises Pro operations without naming any; a context granted a Pro tool's capability also gets that tool's row after it. Call list_coverage for the current state rather than relying on these numbers.

Legacy local recipe paths are limited to the output directory, --imported-store, and repeatable --allow-root directories (also GENEFOX_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS, separated by : on POSIX or ; on Windows). The server resolves links before testing containment, then opens that canonical file without following replacement links. Validation and rendering consume the bytes from that held handle, rather than reopening the model's path. Devices, sockets, FIFOs, directories, and files above 64 MiB are refused with local_path_* codes; the byte ceiling also applies if a file grows while it is read. fetch_url accepts only an allowed public HTTP(S) URL and never turns a file: URL into a local read.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: See Agent plugins for the shared skills, launchers, setup and host configuration.

docs.title: GeneFox agent plugin
docs.text:
This package connects Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode to the genefox mcp server. The server runs public cancer-genomics analyses (TCGA/GDC, GEO, GTEx, CCLE, Treehouse, Expression Atlas, cBioPortal) and writes figures and exports. The package holds the manifests, a launcher, a setup check, and seven shared skills that teach the agent how to use the tools and report their results.

The plugin is Apache-2.0 (see LICENSE and NOTICE). The GeneFox app and the genefox command-line tool are proprietary Vindhya Data Science software and are outside this license. The GeneFox name and logo are not licensed. The plugin bundles no binary and no credentials.

docs.title: CLI setup
docs.text:
This is version 0.1.0 of the plugin. It needs the GeneFox 1.1.0 CLI (or newer) with its resources; the GeneFox documentation describes how to obtain it. You can install the plugin first: when the CLI is missing, the setup skill offers a visible command for your approval:

"<installed-plugin-root>/bin/genefox-install"

On native Windows use "<installed-plugin-root>\bin\genefox-install.cmd". It runs the installer with PowerShell's RemoteSigned execution policy for that process only; your machine's policy is unchanged (a Group Policy setting still takes precedence). If you installed the plugin from a downloaded archive, Windows marks its scripts as coming from the internet and RemoteSigned refuses them: the command stops and prints the exact Unblock-File -LiteralPath ... line for the plugin's two installer scripts (libexec\genefox-plugin-install.ps1 and libexec\install-genefox-cli.ps1). Check that the plugin came from GeneFox, run that line in PowerShell, then run the command again. Claude Code can use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; Codex and OpenCode use the resolved installed path. The launcher and SessionStart hook never download or install anything. Only the explicit installer command downloads the release, verifies GeneFox's pinned minisign signature and SHA-256, installs the CLI, and shows its third-party notice. The default prefix is ~/.local; Windows uses %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\GeneFox and the release installer adds its bin directory to the user PATH. Pass --prefix DIR on POSIX or -Prefix DIR -NoModifyPath on Windows to use another destination. The plugin installer always uses the pinned release location and signing key: it refuses --base and --pubkey-file (-Base, -PubkeyFile or GENEFOX_CLI_BASE on Windows) and every account-helper option; run the release installer yourself for those. The libexec/ release verifiers are source-identical to the repository release installers. After a successful install, restart or reconnect the GeneFox MCP server in your client and run bin/genefox-check. A signed public release must be available; this package contains no CLI binary. You can also supply an existing CLI through GENEFOX_BIN.

bin/genefox-locate.sh finds the binary. It takes the first match in this order:

  1. The file named by GENEFOX_BIN, if it is a regular, executable file.
  2. genefox on PATH.
  3. ~/.local/bin/genefox.
  4. On Windows only, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\GeneFox\bin\genefox.exe (where install-genefox-cli.ps1 installs).
  5. /Applications/GeneFox.app/Contents/Helpers/genefox (the macOS app's embedded copy, when your app version includes it).
  6. ~/Applications/GeneFox.app/Contents/Helpers/genefox.

The macOS app's copy, including the Mac App Store version's, runs in its own App Sandbox. It reads its resources from the app, so it needs no other setup, but it cannot read your working directory, and it writes only to its own container and the GeneFox group container. For that copy the launcher drops a GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR outside the group container, and figures and exports go to ~/Library/Group Containers/6NXG8V2R8W.com.vds.GeneFox/Agent Output/ (the app's Settings shows it in Finder). The standalone CLI has none of these limits. The app finds its resources only when it is installed in /Applications.

If none matches, the launcher offers the bundled explicit installer or GENEFOX_BIN and exits 127.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: The launcher and check are POSIX shell scripts, and bin/genefox-launch.cmd is the launcher's Windows twin, with the same search order (GENEFOX_BIN, genefox.exe on PATH, then %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\GeneFox\bin\genefox.exe) and the same message and exit status 127. No manifest names it. On Windows, Claude Code runs the MCP command ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/genefox-launch without a shell, and the bare name resolves to the .cmd beside the script (verified with Claude Code 2.1.268). The SessionStart hook stays the POSIX genefox-check, because Claude Code runs hook commands through Git Bash on Windows. Keep bin/*.cmd in CRLF; .gitattributes enforces it.

docs.title: Install in Claude Code
docs.text:
Add the public marketplace and install the plugin:

claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/vindhyadatascience/genefox-plugins
claude plugin install genefox@genefox

Inside Claude Code, the equivalent commands are /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/vindhyadatascience/genefox-plugins and /plugin install genefox@genefox. For a local checkout of this public repository, use its root directory as the marketplace source. The marketplace and plugin are both named genefox.

To verify, run claude mcp list and look for the plugin's genefox server, then run /plugin in a session to see the plugin and its skills.

Remove any user-scope genefox MCP entry first, or the agent sees two servers with the same tools:

claude mcp remove genefox

docs.title: Skills and tools
docs.text:
Each skill lists its tools in its own ## Tools section. This table repeats them.

Skill What it does Tools genefox-setup Sets up, checks and troubleshoots the server. account_status, list_coverage, list_operations genefox-tcga-gene One gene in TCGA/GDC cohorts: expression by group, tumor vs normal, pan-cancer, isoforms, cohort and case exploration. tcga_projects, tcga_expression, tcga_tumor_normal, tcga_pan_cancer_expression, tcga_compare_cohorts, tcga_gene_isoforms, tcga_cohort_summary, tcga_cases, tcga_case_detail, tcga_case_expression, tcga_sample_pca genefox-survival Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank and Cox results. tcga_survival, tcga_pan_cancer_survival, geo_survival genefox-differential Multi-gene work: differential expression, heatmaps, top correlates, gene signatures. tcga_differential_expression, tcga_heatmap, tcga_top_correlates, tcga_gene_signature, list_signature_presets, imported_de_enrichment genefox-geo Finds and analyzes GEO series. geo_search, geo_finder_plan, geo_dataset_details, geo_supplementary_layout, geo_series_expression, geo_gene_correlation, geo_top_correlates, geo_heatmap, geo_sample_pca, geo_collection_summary genefox-reference Reference data: GTEx, Human Protein Atlas, CCLE, Treehouse, Expression Atlas, ArrayExpress, ToxicoDB, cBioPortal. gene_info, gtex_tissue_expression, hpa_gene, reference_ccle_expression, reference_treehouse_expression, reference_expression_atlas, reference_expression_atlas_catalog, toxicodb_search, toxicodb_experiments, toxicodb_analysis, arrayexpress_search, arrayexpress_details, arrayexpress_expression, cbioportal_studies, cbioportal_composition, cbioportal_expression, cbioportal_alterations, cbioportal_cross_study_mutations, cbioportal_significantly_mutated_genes, cbioportal_structural_variants, cbioportal_treatment_counts, cbioportal_mutation_burden genefox-reporting How to report results faithfully, and how to plan questions and open app links. open_destination, tcga_ask_plan, tcga_validate_query, geo_ask_plan, tcga_chat_schema, geo_chat_schema

Report files are opt-in: by default the agent answers in the conversation and writes no report or export file, and it offers a report when one would help. When you ask for one, the reporting skill prefers one multipart report for related analyses, assembled by the host from the returned figures and findings, in matching PDF and HTML versions when both can be exported. It keeps each analysis's numbers, sample counts, sources and caveats in its own section. Both versions carry the GeneFox wordmark, product link and the credit "made with GeneFox"; the skill bundles the approved fox artwork, used unmodified as the NOTICE permits, for host-composed reports. Explicit HTML-only or other format requests and separate outputs retain their requested shape. Per-call exports (csv, recipe, html) remain available; html exports one figure with the shared GeneFox brand header and can support a combined report. PDF composition uses the host's document capabilities; analysis tools do not expose a pdf option. Missing output capabilities are disclosed rather than replaced with invented files.

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text:
Tool results can contain text from third parties, such as GEO sample labels and cBioPortal study names. Any field named untrusted_* is data, never instructions. The skills tell the agent to quote such fields as data and to relay numbers, captions, caveats and figure disclosures exactly as returned.

The plugin starts the server with --no-model-tools. The agent host supplies the model; plugins never offer GeneFox's local or cloud model tools. They remain in the GeneFox app and the CLI. GeneFox's deterministic planning aids stay: tcga_ask_plan, geo_ask_plan, tcga_validate_query and the chat schemas give the agent the app's parser, policy and cohort capabilities to work within.

The plugin enables nothing privileged. It pre-approves no tools, so each host keeps its normal permission prompts. The launcher never installs the CLI or passes --enable-legacy-tools or --imported-store; installation requires the explicit command approved by the user. GeneFox Pro needs a linked GeneFox account, which the 1.1.0 CLI cannot use outside the GeneFox app, so the server lists no Pro tools and the plugin cannot grant them; arguments a tool schema marks "GeneFox Pro" are refused. Free tools need no GeneFox login. The server owns the network allowlist, resource integrity and output policy; the GeneFox MCP server guide in the GeneFox documentation describes the full model.

docs.title: Timeouts and output
docs.text:
.mcp.json sets Claude Code's timeout to 960000 ms, and .codex-mcp.json sets Codex's per-tool tool_timeout_sec to 960 seconds (16 minutes). Codex's separate startup_timeout_sec is 30 seconds. OpenCode's opencode/opencode.json sets its per-server timeout to 960000 ms, which bounds every tool call. The server's longest per-call deadline is 900 seconds, leaving 60 seconds of transport margin. Cold calls download and parse large public datasets and can take minutes. A shorter host timeout cuts them off with a request-timed-out error. Claude Code's separate startup limit is MCP_TIMEOUT, for example MCP_TIMEOUT=30000 claude. See the client guide in the GeneFox documentation and Codex MCP settings.

Claude Code writes figures and exports to ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/output through GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR. Codex forwards an explicit GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR and otherwise the shared launcher uses ~/GeneFox/agent-output; its MCP configuration uses a relative launcher and cwd, because Codex does not expand Claude plugin variables there. GeneFox never overwrites existing files. The macOS app's sandboxed copy writes to its group container instead (see the lookup order above).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Run bin/genefox-check from the plugin directory. It prints the binary path and version, runs genefox doctor, and ends with doctor: healthy or doctor: unhealthy. It exits 0 only when the binary is found and doctor passes.
